clue.text: Instruction from teachers, perhaps workers at university

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands or all hands on deck
to be up is to be in residence at university, a British usage

explanation.surface: Someone guesses what a group of academics might tell the staff working at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers at university' reads as campus staff, but it splits into two pieces. Being 'up' means being at university in British English, as in going up to Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers asking a class to raise their arms before answering give this command, and 'perhaps' flags it as one example.

clue.text: Trendy party with good food

parts.note: hot means fashionable or trendy
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A fashionable gathering serves fine catering.
explanation.definitionFit: A frankfurter in a bread roll is a common example of food, especially at fairs.

clue.text: Expression of relief after one leaves old relative

indicators.note: after places the expression of relief behind what remains of one
leaves means the letter for old departs from the word one

parts.note: taken as written before a letter leaves it
phew is what people say when relieved

explanation.surface: Someone sighs with relief once an elderly relation departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old relative' tempts as one phrase, but 'old' is the letter that 'leaves' removes and 'relative' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family member, so he counts as a relative.

clue.text: Doctor cures nits accepting I go over with a fine-toothed comb

definitions.text: go over with a fine-toothed comb

indicators.note: accepting means the rearranged letters take the letter I inside them
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of cures nits are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic treats head lice and agrees to comb through a child's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' rearranges CURES NITS, and 'accepting' puts I inside. The nit comb in the surface makes the definition look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To go over something with a fine-toothed comb is an idiom for examining it in close detail.

clue.text: Satisfaction from parking on trip

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the letter for parking on top of the word for trip

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure from finding a parking spot on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride is the pleasure or contentment felt in an achievement, a synonym for satisfaction.

clue.text: Job in the morning going round neighbourhood, primarily?

definitions.text: Job in the morning going round neighbourhood, primarily?

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: going round means the letters for the morning turn about and are read backwards

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks times in the morning

indicators.note: primarily signals that only the first letter of neighbourhood is taken

explanation.surface: A description of someone whose work is an early round of the local streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses the morning abbreviation. The whole clue also describes the person who delivers letters on a morning round of the neighbourhood, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail carrier's work is a morning round of local streets delivering letters, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Port I pour out — it might have a nice bouquet

definitions.text: it might have a nice bouquet

indicators.note: out means the letters of Port I pour are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone serving fortified wine says the drink has a fine nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' suggests the aroma of wine, but it is a floral scent: the definition is a bowl of dried petals.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of dried petals and spices kept for its fragrance gives a pleasant scent, its bouquet.

clue.text: Wrong king's flag

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess; the 's joins it to the definition

explanation.surface: A monarch's banner is the wrong one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning weaken or droop.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or decline, as spirits can droop and fall.

clue.text: Keep most important article in metal container

parts.note: main means principal or most important

indicators.note: in means the article is placed inside the container

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Store the crucial item inside a metal box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside TIN, giving TAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going or in good repair is to preserve it, matching this verb.

clue.text: Hot, upset with new record in son's game

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for hot upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: hot and in both mean fashionable
an EP, an extended play, is a record
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy's game is disrupted by fresh music and the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' here means fashionable, and 'upset' turns it backwards since this is a down clue; the clue's own 'in' is used as written.
explanation.definitionFit: This skittles game, played by bowling at a set of wooden pins, is an example of a game.

clue.text: Animal hit with anger, almost

parts.note: to tap is to hit lightly

indicators.note: almost means the word for anger loses its final letter

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A creature lashes out furiously, or nearly does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims IRE to IR.
explanation.definitionFit: This hoofed mammal with a short trunk, from South America and Asia, is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Where camper might be if female's abandoned on purpose

parts.note: a camper might be in a tent, written as one run of letters

indicators.note: abandoned means the letter for female is dropped from the word if

parts.note: taken as written before its letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a woman left a campsite deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' looks like a phrase meaning deliberately, but 'on' is a piece and 'purpose' alone is the definition. 'abandoned' takes F from IF, leaving I.
explanation.definitionFit: A purpose is an aim or plan, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Exaggerated where Tommy had to go?

definitions.meaning: excessive, far beyond what is reasonable
Tommy is the nickname for a British soldier; in the First World War soldiers climbed out of the trenches and across the parapet to attack

explanation.surface: A soldier's grim duty is described alongside a word for overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins is the traditional name for an ordinary British soldier. The second reading is literal: the place a trench soldier went when ordered to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for overdone behaviour came from the trench phrase for leaving cover to charge the enemy.

clue.text: Second best bar

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: The runner-up among the finest pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is a verb meaning prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to block or prevent it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Dumb — like a forgetful politician?

definitions.meaning: unable to say anything, as when struck dumb
a politician who forgot the prepared address would have none to give

explanation.surface: An insult aimed at a politician who forgot what to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a politician without their address. The question mark marks the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dumb in the old sense means mute, lost for words through shock or emotion.

clue.text: Pause at home and print route out

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of print route are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone stops at home to print directions for a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PRINT ROUTE into TERRUPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a break in something continuing, like a halt in a conversation.

clue.text: I tailored new item from a rag

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of I tailored are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tailor makes a fresh garment out of an old cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag' looks like a scrap of cloth but is slang for a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article giving a newspaper's opinion is a piece found in a paper, which is called a rag.

clue.text: Bear ought to run after European

indicators.note: after places the letter for run behind the letter for European

parts.note: should means ought to
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A bear ought to chase after a European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning carry or take on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a burden or responsibility is to take it on, as one carries a load.

clue.text: Tango is bubbly and cold? One's doubtful

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing about, so the letters of Tango is are mixed up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether a fizzy, chilled orange soft drink is any good; Tango is a British brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' rearranges TANGO IS. Tango is a fizzy orange drink sold in Britain, which makes the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that God's existence cannot be known is a doubter about religion.

clue.text: Excellent alcohol and Edward's cheerful

parts.note: high means of excellent quality, as in high standards
spirit is strong alcohol such as gin or whisky
Ed is short for Edward; the 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: Edward is in a good mood after some fine liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lively and in good spirits is merry and full of energy, matching cheerful.

clue.text: Sailing vessel, say, with 100 on

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the numeral on top of the word for say

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A boat, for instance, carrying a hundred people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' attached to the vessel, but it is the verb UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A small single-masted boat, or a fast patrol boat, is a type of sailing vessel.

clue.text: Expression from Romeo entering stage

indicators.note: entering means the letter for Romeo goes inside the word for stage

parts.note: a phase is a stage in a process
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A line spoken by Romeo as he walks on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' looks theatrical but means a step in a process.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression is a group of words such as an idiom, the same as this word.

clue.text: Buffoons regularly picked out flying saucers

indicators.note: regularly picked out signals taking every other letter of Buffoons, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Clowns are chosen at intervals to spot alien craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of Buffoons are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying saucers are the classic picture of unidentified flying objects, so the abbreviation fits.

clue.text: Number hurry after the tailless bird

indicators.note: after places the word for hurry behind the shortened the

parts.note: a number is a song or piece of music

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the word the is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before it loses its end
to rush is to hurry

explanation.surface: A musical item hurries along behind a bird that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the tailless bird' suggests a bird without a tail, but 'tailless' trims only the word 'the', and 'after' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This speckled songbird of Europe is a species of the thrush family, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Grand English actor's gluttony

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
Oliver Reed was a famous English actor; the 's joins him to the definition

explanation.surface: A famous English actor's appetite for excess.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Reed was an English film actor known for hard living, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is an excessive desire for food, a form of insatiable wanting.

clue.text: Worry about appearing in newspaper

indicators.note: appearing in means the word for about is placed inside the newspaper's letters

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Anxiety over appearing in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry about' reads as one phrase, but 'about' is a piece placed inside the Financial Times by 'appearing in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious and agitated, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stop this writer's influence

parts.note: to deter is to stop or discourage
this writer means the setter, so this writer's means mine

explanation.surface: A columnist asks readers to resist the sway of their writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the setter speaking of themselves, so their possession is MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence is to shape or decide an outcome, as one factor can settle another.

clue.text: Over time gathering ten tonnes

indicators.note: gathering means the word for time takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: an era is a period of time
X is the Roman numeral for ten
T is the abbreviation for tonnes

explanation.surface: A period stretching past its limit while collecting heavy loads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' puts XT inside ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over is surplus or additional, beyond what is needed, as in 'left over'.

clue.text: Reading unsettling article

indicators.note: unsettling means the letters of article are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is studying a disturbing piece in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the activity of the surface, but it is the definition: a reading given to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading is a performance of poetry or prose before an audience, a sense this word shares.

clue.text: Earn editor's backing and be good enough

indicators.note: backing means the letters for editor are reversed

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor; the 's attaches the backing to it
to serve is to be adequate, as in 'that will serve'

explanation.surface: A journalist earns the editor's support by doing adequate work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to merit it through effort or qualities, a direct synonym.
